observations: A head shape built from overlapping purple and dark blue contour lines sits against a flat salmon-pink background, tilted slightly left.
Bright cyan, yellow, green, and white strokes fill and surround the head, with a tight spiral of blue and orange lines forming a vortex at center-left.
Loose diagonal hatching in pink and white crosses the background at upper-left and lower-right, bleeding into the figure's edges and dissolving its boundary.
reading: The head emerges less as a solid form than as a collision of colored scribbles competing for the same space. A spiral near the center reads as an eye socket, pulling attention inward, while slashing cyan and white lines at the crown scatter it outward. The salmon field, warm and unbroken at the edges, makes the tangled interior feel pressurized—lines pushing against a soft, quiet container. The mood can feel frantic or playful depending on where you focus.
contextAngle: In the owned Scrimshaw numbered family, this work sits between Scrimshaw8 and Scrimshaw12. Where Scrimshaw8 uses heavy black outlines to anchor its head, Scrimshaw9 drops black almost entirely, letting purple and blue contours carry the structure alone.

connections.reason: Both show a single head built from layered scribble lines, but Scrimshaw8 relies on thick black strokes over a yellow ground while Scrimshaw9 replaces black with purple on salmon.
The tight spiral marking the eye in Scrimshaw9 echoes the yellow spiral eye in nnxyz nnotb #264, a shared shorthand for a face's focal point across two different artists.

lookingQuestion: Where does the purple outline separate from the blue and white lines enough to suggest a jaw or chin, and where do those boundaries dissolve completely?
ambiguities: Whether the diagonal hatching at upper-left is background texture or part of the head's hair area is unclear from the image alone.
The spiral form reads as an eye but could also be an ear or purely abstract mark; no supporting evidence confirms either reading.
